'''Stanley Fields''' is an American [[biologist]] best known for developing the [[yeast two hybrid]] method for identifying protein–protein interactions.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal
| volume = 340
| title = A novel genetic system to detect protein-protein interactions
| issue = 6230
| pages = 245–246
| journal = Nature | first2 = O.
| last2 = Song
| pmid = 2547163
| year = 1989
| last1 = Fields | first1 = S.
| doi = 10.1038/340245a0 
|bibcode = 1989Natur.340..245F | s2cid = 4320733
}}</ref> He is currently a professor of Genome Sciences at the [[University of Washington]] and [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]] Investigator,<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1534/genetics.114.165134| pmid = 24939989| title = Would Fred Sanger Get Funded Today?| journal = Genetics| volume = 197| issue = 2| pages = 435–439| year = 2014| last1 = Fields | first1 = Stanley| authorlink1 = Stanley Fields (biologist)| pmc=4063904}}</ref><ref name="scopus">{{Scopus|id=7102919472}}</ref> and previously served as chair of the Department of Genome Sciences.<ref>{{Cite web |title=UW Genome Sciences: Stanley Fields |url=https://www.gs.washington.edu/faculty/fields.htm |access-date=2023-08-14 |website=www.gs.washington.edu}}</ref>

==Education==
Fields was educated at the University of Cambridge where he was awarded a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] in 1981 for research carried out in the [[Laboratory of Molecular Biology]] with [[Greg Winter]] and [[George Brownlee]].<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1038/292072a0| pmid = 7278968| title = Nucleotide sequence of the haemagglutinin gene of a human influenza virus H1 subtype| journal = Nature| volume = 292| issue = 5818| pages = 72–75| year = 1981| last1 = Winter | first1 = G. | authorlink1 = Greg Winter| last2 = Fields | first2 = S. | authorlink2 = Stanley Fields (biologist)| last3 = Brownlee | first3 = G. G. | authorlink3 = George Brownlee| bibcode = 1981Natur.292...72W| s2cid = 4312205}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1038/290213a0| pmid = 7010182| title = Structure of the neuraminidase gene in human influenza virus A/PR/8/34| journal = Nature| volume = 290| issue = 5803| pages = 213–217| year = 1981| last1 = Fields | first1 = S. | authorlink1 = Stanley Fields (biologist)| last2 = Winter | first2 = G. | authorlink2 = Greg Winter| last3 = Brownlee | first3 = G. G. | authorlink3 = George Brownlee| bibcode = 1981Natur.290..213F| s2cid = 8051512}}</ref>

==Research==
Fields developed the [[Two-hybrid screening|yeast two-hybrid system]] in 1989,<ref name=":0" /> which has been widely used by Fields<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bartel |first1=P. L. |last2=Roecklein |first2=J. A. |last3=SenGupta |first3=D. |last4=Fields |first4=S. |date=January 1996 |title=A protein linkage map of Escherichia coli bacteriophage T7 |journal=Nature Genetics |volume=12 |issue=1 |pages=72–77 |doi=10.1038/ng0196-72 |issn=1061-4036 |pmid=8528255}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Iwabuchi |first1=K. |last2=Li |first2=B. |last3=Bartel |first3=P. |last4=Fields |first4=S. |date=June 1993 |title=Use of the two-hybrid system to identify the domain of p53 involved in oligomerization |journal=Oncogene |volume=8 |issue=6 |pages=1693–1696 |issn=0950-9232 |pmid=8502489}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Schwikowski |first1=B. |last2=Uetz |first2=P. |last3=Fields |first3=S. |date=December 2000 |title=A network of protein-protein interactions in yeast |journal=Nature Biotechnology |volume=18 |issue=12 |pages=1257–1261 |doi=10.1038/82360 |issn=1087-0156 |pmid=11101803|s2cid=3009359 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Iwabuchi |first1=K. |last2=Bartel |first2=P. L. |last3=Li |first3=B. |last4=Marraccino |first4=R. |last5=Fields |first5=S. |date=1994-06-21 |title=Two cellular proteins that bind to wild-type but not mutant p53 |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America |volume=91 |issue=13 |pages=6098–6102 |doi=10.1073/pnas.91.13.6098 |doi-access=free |issn=0027-8424 |pmid=8016121|pmc=44145 |bibcode=1994PNAS...91.6098I }}</ref> and others to identify protein-protein interactions in various organisms and biological contexts.

Along with [[Matt Kaeberlein]] and [[Brian K. Kennedy|Brian Kennedy]],  in later work Fields has carried out genome-wide screens for aging genes in yeast.  Kaeberlein and co-workers have questioned the hypothesis that lifespan extension from [[caloric restriction]] is mediated by [[Sirtuins]].<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1371/journal.pbio.0020296| pmid = 15328540| title = Sir2-Independent Life Span Extension by Calorie Restriction in Yeast| journal = PLOS Biology| volume = 2| issue = 9| pages = e296| year = 2004| last1 = Kaeberlein | first1 = M. | last2 = Kirkland | first2 = K. T. | last3 = Fields | first3 = S. | last4 = Kennedy | first4 = B. K. | pmc=514491| doi-access = free}}</ref>  Instead Kaeberlein, Fields, and Kennedy have proposed that [[caloric restriction]] increases lifespan by decreasing the activity of the [[Mammalian target of rapamycin|Target of Rapamycin (TOR) kinase]].<ref>{{Cite journal
